deskyard forward: map TCP ports between this machine and the environment

Usage: deskyard [-e NAME] forward [-R] PORT[:PORT]...

Maps TCP ports both ways until Ctrl-C, over the remote access API (no port is
opened anywhere else). Each argument is one mapping. PORT or LOCAL:ENV: this
machine's 127.0.0.1:LOCAL becomes localhost:ENV in the environment (a dev
server here, reachable by the environment's browser). -R PORT or -R ENV:LOCAL
(reverse; one -R before each such mapping): the environment's localhost:ENV
becomes 127.0.0.1:LOCAL here. Both ends listen on loopback only; the
environment won't listen below 1024 (plain forward only; -R just dials, so -R
80:8080 works). A port in use on either side fails that mapping, which is
retried, and the others carry on. When the connection drops (the environment
stops or restarts, the network blips) it keeps its local listeners, closes
open connections and reconnects with backoff (1 s up to 30 s). It exits only
on Ctrl-C, or when the token is refused. Run it in the background. Inside an
environment it needs -e too.

Arguments:
  PORT       string...   required  a mapping: PORT or LOCAL:ENV; after -R, PORT or ENV:LOCAL

Options:
  -R, --reverse        the next mapping is reverse: a port in the environment
                       becomes a port here

Prints: one line per mapping each time it goes live: "in LOCAL ENV" or "out
  ENV 127.0.0.1:LOCAL"; on stderr one line per state change (linked,
  lost and retrying, port in use)

Examples:
  deskyard -e alice forward 3000 -R 5173
  deskyard -e alice forward 8080:3000 &
  deskyard -e alice forward -R 9229:19229

Where: on the chosen environment (-e NAME); inside an environment too, since it maps ports between two machines. Ports are LOCAL:ENV, or ENV:LOCAL after -R. The environment won't listen below 1024. "Linked to ..." and the out lines appear when the link is accepted, before the environment side is known to run
Exit codes: 0 after Ctrl-C, 1 when the token is refused (401) or no remote is set up, 2 usage error
